experiments.title: freeze duration x freeze depth
experiments.note: The shock on its own, against a world with neither AI nor freeze. Both axes are swept, so the baseline is one fixed reference for the whole grid rather than a per-cell twin.

experiments.title: freeze depth x aiDampeningAbove
experiments.note: Freeze fixed at 5 years. Gamma_above acts on people already at their institution's teaching level, i.e. the seniors a thinned field leans on.

experiments.title: freeze depth x aiDampeningBelow
experiments.note: Freeze fixed at 5 years. The central pairing: gamma_below is the channel AI crowds out entrant learning through, and a freeze removes entrants outright, so the two act on the same population from opposite directions.

experiments.title: freeze depth x aiLevelFraction
experiments.note: Freeze fixed at 5 years. Lambda sets how much of the field counts as below the AI; a freeze changes the shape of the field, so it changes who that is.

notesPage.title: Recruitment shock set: definitions and method
notesPage.html:
Scope

The set applies a temporary reduction in hiring to a field that has already reached its equilibrium distribution, crossed with freeze duration, freeze depth, and each of the three AI parameters in turn.

Timing

Horizon 2640 ticks (one tick is one month), so 220 years. The freeze is applied at t = 1440 (year 120 = 3 careers at the 40-year career length used throughout), not at t = 0: mean expertise and expert share reach their stationary band within about one career and hold it flat afterward on this calibration; system capability has a slower initial ramp, driven by the tenure structure rather than by mean expertise, that levels out by roughly year 100. An earlier freeze risks measuring the shock against a population still moving on its own rather than against an equilibrium; both the start (--shock-start-years) and the aftermath length (--aftermath-years) are flags to the generator, not fixed choices baked into this text. In the pairings that fix duration at 5 years, the freeze runs from month 1441 to month 1500 (year 125). Where duration is itself an axis, the freeze runs from month 1441 for 12Y months. 100 years remain after the freeze ends in every case.

Mechanism

For the duration of the freeze, a fraction of retirements are refilled and the remainder leave the post vacant; that fraction is recruitmentFraction, shown in the report as hiring retained. 0 is a total freeze; 1 is normal hiring. The axis is therefore ordered from most severe (0) to least (1), the reverse of a severity axis.

There is no catch-up hiring. After the freeze, retirements are refilled at the normal rate, which does not exceed replacement, so vacancies opened during the freeze are not recovered and the headcount reduction is permanent for the remainder of the run. This keeps two effects separable: removal of a cohort from the expertise ladder, and reduction in field size.

Baseline

Unlike the other sets, in which the baseline arm differs from the treatment arm only in aiEnabled, this baseline also sets recruitmentShockYears = 0 (baselineParams). The baseline is therefore a field with neither AI nor the freeze. Change panels report the combined effect of both; level panels are read from the treatment arm, since the baseline's headcount is 1.0 by construction and carries no information about the freeze.

Design

4 experiments. The first varies freeze duration (1 to 10 years) against freeze depth. The remaining three fix duration at 5 years and vary depth against aiDampeningAbove, aiDampeningBelow, and aiLevelFraction respectively. Each is a grid at 32 replicates. Total 27,520 runs.

Metrics

Mean expertise is not the primary metric for this set. The freeze removes entrants, who are the lowest-expertise members of the field, so mean expertise among the remaining population can be stable or increase while the field is losing headcount. Headcount retained and capability per head are reported together to distinguish two outcomes: a smaller field with unchanged per-head capability, against a field that has also lost teaching capacity. A ratio of 1.0 on capability-per-head indicates the former; a ratio below 1.0 indicates the latter.

Values are taken at the tick selected above, averaged over 32 replicates. Baseline and treatment arms of a replicate share a seed. The two arms diverge in their random draw sequence once the freeze changes how many draws a tick consumes, so replicate variance in this set is higher than in a set where the arms differ only by a multiplier. Population statistics are computed over staffed posts; a vacant post is excluded, not counted as zero expertise.
